Referred from: UPHC Savli with referral slip.
Brought by ASHA worker and father.

Diagnosis: Dengue fever (NS1 antigen positive) with thrombocytopenia

Chief Complaints:
Fever with chills x 5 days, body pains, retro-orbital pain, vomiting x 2 days.

History of Present Illness:
Patient was apparently normal 5 days back when he developed high grade fever with chills, associated with myalgia and retro-orbital pain. No h/o bleeding manifestations, malena or haematuria. Not a k/c/o DM/HTN/BA.

Family History: Father aged 95 years, alive, k/c/o HTN.

On Examination:
Temp 101.2 F, PR 102/min, BP 100/70 mmHg, RR 18/min, SpO2 98% on RA. Tourniquet test negative. P/A: soft, mild tenderness in Rt. hypochondrium. CVS: S1S2 +, RS: B/L NVBS, CNS: NAD.

Investigations:
NS1 antigen: Positive. IgM dengue: Negative. Hb 13.8 g/dL, TLC 3,200/cumm, Platelets 38,000/cumm (1,12,000/cumm at discharge). Hct 44%. SGOT/SGPT 112/96 U/L. USG abdomen: mild GB wall oedema.

Course in the Hospital:
Managed conservatively with IV fluids (NS/RL), antipyretics and serial platelet monitoring. No platelet transfusion required. Patient improved symptomatically and has been afebrile for the last 48 hrs.

Medications on Discharge:
1. Tab. Dolo 650 mg 1-1-1 x 3 days (SOS for fever)
2. Tab. Pan 40 mg 1-0-0 before food x 5 days
3. ORS 1 sachet in 1 litre water, sip frequently

Advice: Avoid NSAIDs (Brufen/Combiflam). Plenty of oral fluids. Repeat CBC after 3 days.
Follow up in General Medicine OPD (Room No. 16) on 20/12/2024.
